title: Fact vs opinion
keyIdea: A fact is a statement that can be checked: measured, counted, observed or looked up in a reliable source. An opinion is what someone thinks, feels or believes, so it cannot be proved. Judging words such as best, brilliant, should and delicious mark an opinion, and one sentence can hold a fact and an opinion together. Writers, especially in adverts, often dress an opinion up as a fact.

kid: Ask one question: could I check it? "A blue whale can grow to about 30 metres long" can be checked in a book or with a tape. That is a fact. "Whales are the most amazing animals" cannot. Someone else may love tigers more. That is an opinion.

Look for judging words. Best, worst, brilliant, boring, should and delicious all tell you what someone thinks. A number does not make a sentence a fact. "The top five goals were all spectacular" still has the judging word spectacular.

A surprising fact is still a fact. Sharks were on Earth before trees. It sounds odd, but fossils let scientists check it. A fact can also turn out to be wrong when someone checks it. It is still the kind of statement you can test.

Writers mix the two. "Our school has 400 pupils, so it is far too crowded" has a fact, then a view. Adverts go further. They say "it is a fact that" or "everyone knows", or use sure words like clearly. None of that makes a view checkable.
adult: The English national curriculum for Years 5 and 6 asks pupils to tell statements of fact from opinion when they read. Here they label each statement in a non-fiction text. They explain how they can tell. They also spot tricks that make a view look like a fact.

The test is: can it be checked? A fact can be measured, counted, seen or looked up in a source you trust. An opinion is a judgement, a feeling or a belief, so fair people can disagree. Judging words (best, brilliant), words like should and must, and phrases like I think are the usual signs.

Common mistakes: thinking any sentence with a number is a fact; calling a strange or new fact an opinion; thinking a view held by lots of people becomes a fact; labelling a whole sentence when only one part judges; and trusting an advert that says "it is a fact that". Another slip is calling a false claim an opinion. A false claim can still be checked. It just fails the check.

In the lab the learner swipes statements into fact and opinion, taps the judging word in four sentences, and colours the fact part and the view part of mixed sentences. Then they tag three advert tricks and colour a whole news report.

visual.caption: Can each statement be checked? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Chess is more fun than football.
London is the capital of the UK.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: swipe statements, find the judging word, split mixed sentences, tag advert tricks and highlight a news report.

practice.prompt: "The school trip costs £{n}." Is this a fact or an opinion?
practice.hint: Could you check it? Look at the letter from school or ask the office.
practice.explain: It is a fact. You can check the price of £{n} on the letter. There is no judging word.

practice.prompt: "The {n} best songs of the year are all by one band." Fact or opinion?
practice.hint: The number {n} can be counted. But is "best" something you can check?
practice.explain: It is an opinion. "Best" is a judgement, and the number {n} does not change that. Another listener would pick different songs.

practice.prompt: Which word makes this an opinion? "The museum, which opened in 1990, is wonderful."
practice.hint: Which word tells you what the writer thinks?
practice.explain: Wonderful is the judging word. "Opened in 1990" can be checked, so that part is a fact.

practice.prompt: An advert says: "It is a fact that Zing is the tastiest drink." What is it?
choices: An opinion dressed as a fact
A fact, because it says so
A fact, because many people buy it
practice.explain: It is an opinion. Saying "it is a fact that" does not make tastiest checkable. Taste is a judgement.

choices: Bats should be kept as pets.
pool.hint: Which one could a scientist check?
pool.explain: "Bats are mammals" is a fact: bats feed their young on milk. Creepy is a feeling, and should is a view about what ought to happen.

pool.prompt: "Our town has {n} parks, and they are all beautiful." What is this sentence?
pool.hint: Split it into two parts. Check each part on its own.
pool.explain: "Our town has {n} parks" can be counted, so it is a fact. "They are all beautiful" is a view. The sentence holds both.

pool.prompt: "Everyone knows that cats are better than dogs." Fact or opinion?
choices: Fact, because it is about animals
pool.explain: It is an opinion. "Everyone knows" is a trick to make a view sound certain, and better is a judgement.

pool.prompt: Why is "Water freezes at 0 °C" a fact?
choices: It can be checked with a thermometer
It is written in a sure way
pool.hint: What makes any statement a fact?
pool.explain: It can be tested with ice and a thermometer. Belief and a confident tone do not make a fact; being checkable does.

pool.prompt: Which word turns this into an opinion? "The match lasted {n} minutes and was thrilling."
pool.hint: Which word tells you how the writer felt?
pool.explain: Thrilling is the judging word. The {n} minutes can be checked with a clock, so that part is a fact.

pool.prompt: "Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system." Fact or opinion?
choices: Opinion, because hottest is a judging word
pool.hint: Hottest here is measured with instruments, not felt.
pool.explain: It is a fact. Space probes measured Venus at about 465 °C, hotter than Mercury. Hottest is a measurement here, not a taste.

pool.prompt: A report says: "Clearly, the new road is a terrible idea." What does "clearly" do?
choices: Turns the view into a fact
pool.hint: Did the writer give any evidence?
pool.explain: Clearly makes the view sound sure. Terrible is still a judgement, and nothing was checked.
